newsitem.title: UK: UK's OFWAT, Utd Utilities agree Norweb plan.
newsitem.headline: UK's OFWAT, Utd Utilities agree Norweb plan.

text.p: UK water industry regulator OFWAT has agreed proposals with United Utilities Plc to protect the interests of customers of the company's North West Water unit, OFWAT said on Monday.
The proposed licence amendments require North West Water to conduct its business as though it were substantially the company's only business and the company were a separate plc.
They also require United to ensure that North West Water's board has two non-executive directors who have the experience and understanding to represent customers' views to the board and the company.
The moves build on initial changes made two years ago when regional electricity company NORWEB was taken over by North West Water's parent company, in the UK's first multi-utility merger.

"I am pleased that North West Water has agreed these proposals which will achieve a sensible consistency of approach to regulation of the new band of multi-utilities," said Ian Byatt, director general of water services.
Byatt noted that the company had already appointed two non-executive directors to its board.
